assertion_audit.fails_if: The crash fixture reaches _finish with an error or a phase other than PROMOTED; fixture synchronization rather than recovery proof.
The injected BaseException does not escape the first service attempt, so the restart simulation did not occur.
The callback failed to remove its live pointer, a service receipt was published before the injected interruption, or the unfinished request was not retained as RUNNING.
The fake callback did not persist exactly its supplied row; a setup/propagation check whose expected row is the same object provided to the writer.
The fresh service does not adopt the interrupted request exactly once on its first pass.
Restoring the unconditional runs.read_pointer call makes both parameterized cases report promotion-refused; the recorded reversed-commit control demonstrates this failure.
Recovery drops or changes the callback-supplied commit; propagation only, because the expected fixture SHA also seeds the ledger row.
Recovery does not identify an already completed promotion, repeats the review callback, or rewrites the persisted ledger bytes.
Successful recovery retains its request, leaves a false session failure obligation, or lets a new service adopt the completed request again.
The known-present neighbor row is unreadable/altered, or the absent-row fixture already contains a subject row; these validate test inputs.
Accepting an absent or mismatched ledger row yields success instead of refusal, loses the corresponding diagnostic, or fails to project the refusal to this session.

evidence_caveats: Review scope is only commits since the preceding reviewed head; previous findings are not re-reviewed wholesale.
New recovery tests use real ledger IO and pointer deletion with injected review callbacks; they do not rerun full acceptance policy.
No suite rerun; read the source run receipts, including red controls and all four explicit refusals.
Importer delta receipt reports the same 40 baseline and head failures with zero added IDs; required added_failure_count derives specifically from baseline_suite and after_suite.
MCP plan read reported storage-slow; the live plan was read directly from its canonical HTML.

findings.text: non-blocking: The recovered commit is compared with repository.sha, which the fake callback itself writes into the ledger at lines 507-518; together with the planted-row checks at lines 540 and 573 this proves propagation and fixture setup, not independent identity of a real promoted commit, so preserve the earlier real-receipt evidence and do not count this as new commit-identity coverage.
